root.symptom: W4 ladder OBSERVED: Canvas.drawBitmap of an IN-MEMORY bitmap (Bitmap.createBitmap + Canvas(bitmap).drawColor) RECORDED the op but produced 0 app-owned pixels; resource-drawable bitmaps composited fine (FishRings provenance).
root.first_divergence: canvas_shadow.cpp Canvas section: `if (!capturing_) return not_handled()` — ALL Canvas ops on a Canvas(Bitmap) target outside the view-draw capture window (the AOSP norm: onCreate-time offscreen rendering) were silently dropped; inside the window they polluted the VIEW op list.
root.law: AOSP graphics/Canvas.java: Canvas(Bitmap) / setBitmap bind the canvas to a bitmap target with its OWN matrix/clip/save state; every op rasterizes eagerly INTO that bitmap; the canvas stays live until release().
root.fix: per-canvas sub-recorder (same op laws, isolated matrix/clip/save state) + eager flush into BitmapStore after each op (replay over a temp SoftwareCanvas wrapping the bitmap pixels, copy-in/copy-out); sync_shared_state mirrors Paint/Path state (Paint/Path dispatch never routes to the sub-recorder); re-arm capturing_ after each flush (replay() closes the VIEW capture, but a bitmap canvas is not a frame); getWidth/getHeight answer bitmap dims; bindBitmap of unknown/empty bitmap = honest warn_noop (AOSP would throw).
root.second_root_found_and_fixed_same_wave: flush_bitmap_canvas originally left the sub-recorder dead: replay() ends with capturing_=false (view-frame lifecycle law) so every op after the first flush hit not_handled (probe row R2 proved it: save/translate/drawRect dropped). Fix: re-arm capturing_=true after every flush — a bitmap canvas stays live for its object lifetime (AOSP Canvas lifetime law).
